As of 320 PM Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 1... Patchy dense fog will be possible late tonight and 
early Friday morning across mainly the Coastal Plain and eastern 
Sandhills.

As winds go very light to calm in many spots, more fog and very low 
stratus will be possible late tonight into early Friday morning 
across portions of central NC, mainly to the east of US Highway 1. 
Given the surface high will be centered farther offshore than this 
morning, southerly flow around the high will bring more moist air in 
the low levels from the Atlantic into those locations, with dew 
points increasing to the mid-to-upper-60s. Thus model guidance 
depicts a stronger signal for more widespread fog, locally dense, 
reaching farther NW into our area compared to this morning. Any fog 
will quickly dissipate after sunrise.

KEY MESSAGE 2... Temperatures will remain well above average ahead 
of a cold front that will move south across central NC on Saturday.

A sub-tropical high currently centered near the coast of the 
Carolinas will progress offshore today and settle across the 
southwestern North Atlantic through the weekend. 

At the surface, a ~1020 mb high now centered about halfway between 
Bermuda and the NC coast will drift to near Bermuda, while extending 
westward into the Southeast US, through Friday. Subsidence from the 
subtropical ridge aloft, and southerly, "return" flow around the 
Bermuda surface high, will contribute to additional warming of the 
airmass over the Carolinas and another day of summerlike 
temperatures on Friday. Low-level thicknesses should be about 5-10 m 
higher compared to today, favoring high temperatures in the upper-
80s to lower-90s. Fortunately, Friday afternoon humidity levels will 
again remain relatively low in the 40s percent courtesy of dewpoints 
mixing out to the lower-to-mid-60s. Still, the NWS Experimental 
HeatRisk is forecast to be Moderate across most of the region, 
meaning those who are sensitive to heat, especially those without 
cooling/hydration, are affected. Lows will also be above normal, in 
the lower-to-mid-60s tonight and in the mid-60s to 70 on Friday 
night.

KEY MESSAGE 3... Cloudy, much cooler, and periods of wet conditions 
will develop in cold air damming later Sat through the weekend.

Not a whole lot of change from the previous forecast. Still expect a 
positively-tilted srn stream trough/shear axis to progress slowly 
across the Southeast and Carolinas this weekend, just downstream and 
equatorward of a series of prominent shortwaves that will progress 
through a broad trough that will become centered over ern Canada. 
One nrn stream s/w will amplify as it tracks ewd across the nrn 
Plains and upper MS Valley on Sat and across the Great Lakes and the 
nrn mid-Atlantic/Northeast US Sat night and Sun. Expect a period of 
enhanced lift as the s/w energy interacts with the trough/shear axis 
over the region. The upper trough should amplify swd over the 
Eastern Seaboard on Mon before shifting ewd and offshore Mon night. 

At the surface, a front will settle swd across central NC Fri 
night/Sat, becoming quasi-stationary across SC and southeastern NC 
Sat night. A weak frontal wave is expected to lift newd along the 
boundary on Sun/Sun night, which may help the front retreat north 
and west a bit. Cool, strengthening high pressure will ridge swd 
into the area in the wake of the front Sat/Sat night as it 
progresses ewd from the Great Lakes to the Canadian Maritimes. A 
brief period of CAD may develop over the region Sat night, possibly 
lingering through Sun, especially with the expected rainfall acting 
to lock in the wedge across the NW Sun/Sun night.

With all of the above in mind, expect rain to start Sat afternoon as 
isentropic lift increases within the trough/shear axis and ahead of 
the aforementioned s/w aloft and atop surface ridging, which will 
help lock in a CAD airmass. Rain should continue through Sun 
eve/night when the frontal wave finally moves away from the Carolina 
coast. There is still some uncertainty wrt overall rainfall totals, 
but generally expect 1-2 inches across central NC from Sat aft to 
Sun night. The WPC has central NC in a Marginal Risk for excessive 
rainfall on Sunday. 

If the CAD does indeed lock in, and with the expected rainfall, 
temperatures over the weekend will need to be adjusted downward 
further.

A reinforcing cold front will move across the area Mon eve/night, 
with cool Canadian high pressure building in behind it and dry 
weather expected through mid-week.
